coverageNote: Disk enumeration matched the expected 10 units / 57 files exactly (9 sub-domain directories plus the domain directory itself; every directory contains exactly one *-index.md and one *-cx.md; no directory lacks an index; no non-.md files). The corpus is 1.17 MB of dense prose (~9,000 substantive lines), which exceeds what can be read verbatim in one context. Method used instead: (a) exhaustive programmatic checks over all 57 files for Open-Question tracking well-formedness (177 rows), structural compliance, section presence in every leaf, cross-reference resolvability (all 07.* ids), relative-link resolution, and quantified-threshold collision across the whole corpus; (b) full-fidelity reads of the normative sections (Overview, Behavior, Happy Path, Edge Cases, States, Decisions, Cross-Cut Map, Cross-Cut Details, Rejected Pairs, Open Questions) for the domain root, all nine sub-domain index and CX files, and every [DEEP]/Must leaf; (c) targeted full reads of [PARTIAL] and [SURFACE] leaves at each candidate defect site. Every candidate finding was then verified by following its cross-references before reporting. MoSCoW status maps cleanly onto depth status (MUST->[DEEP], SHOULD->[PARTIAL], COULD/WONT->[SURFACE]) per the ideation-index policy that Won't nodes are 'intentionally minimal, retained for traceability, not built', so thin [SURFACE] leaves were not scored as gaps. Freshness gate observed: nothing under .memory/wiki/specs/audits/ was read other than this output path.

findings.claim: Two decisions in the same Decisions table of 07.06.02 state different, mutually incompatible interaction budgets for the same close-prompt moment, and the file's own Happy Path contradicts one of them. No marker reconciles them.
findings.evidence: 07.06.02-session-close-capture-prompt.md:217 — '| D-06 | One screen, one tap, four seconds. Nothing else rides along | Per DT-06 — every added field cuts completion. Cited by `07.06.04` D-05 as the reason the gear sheet is excluded. |'  CONTRADICTED BY 07.06.02-session-close-capture-prompt.md:220 — '| D-09 | **The moment has a fixed budget, ordered by perishability**: Tier 0 silent (0 interactions) · Tier 1 contributor asks ≤ 5 s, ungated, ≤ 2 taps each · Tier 2 **at most one** Producer heavyweight ask, ≤ 8 interactions / ≤ 90 s · Tier 3 everything else defers |'.  The budget table itself is internally inconsistent in a single row, 07.06.02:84 — '| 1 | **Contributors** | ≤ 5 s after the close signal, **ungated** | **≤ 2 interactions each** | The credit card (`02.02.03` half 1) — one card, one tap |' (≤ 2 interactions AND one tap in the same row).  The Happy Path takes the two-tap reading, 07.06.02:118 — '5. Sam taps confirm while still coiling a cable — **two taps, in the room**; the claim becomes a **verified credit** (`02.04.01`)'.  The States table also takes the two-tap reading, 07.06.02:161 — '| **Populated / Prompting** | Close committed, pre-fill available | Contributors: one card each (≤ 2 taps). Producer: one card, one work (≤ 8 interactions / 90 s) |'.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building the session-close capture prompt asks 'what is the interaction budget?' and gets two answers from the same Decisions table. Following D-06 they build a single-screen, single-tap, four-second card for every actor — which makes the Tier 2 Producer split sheet (specified at ≤ 8 interactions / ≤ 90 s, and owned by 09.02.01) impossible to render at all, silently dropping the split-capture ask that domain D-03 calls the mechanism by which the thesis becomes a product. Following D-09 they build a 2-tap contributor card and an 8-interaction Producer sheet, and D-06's 'one tap, four seconds' is simply false. Two competent implementers reading independently ship different prompts.

AUTHORITATIVE DECISION — 07.04.02-canonical-version-resolver.md:239 — '| D-03 | **Resolution happens once, at the act, and pins there.** Live resolution exists only where the question literally is "what is canonical right now" — the panel | Per DT-04, **revised**. Under revised D-03 almost nothing resolves live — share links (07.05.02 D-02), approvals (07.05.04 D-01) and handoff packages (07.08.01 D-03) all pin at the act. The result is a review link whose audio silently changes after it was sent, which 07.05.02 D-02 names as 'the `FINAL_v3` disease in the highest-stakes context' and which the whole sub-domain exists to prevent. findings.claim: Two adjacent rows of the same Edge Cases table in 07.05.02 give different audio-stop semantics for the identical trigger (link revoked mid-listen): one says the current media segment finishes with an audible stop within 10 s, the next says audio dies immediately. The file's States table and both governing decisions support only the 10 s reading.
findings.evidence: 07.05.02-private-share-links-listen-analytics.md:101 — '| Link **revoked** mid-listen | Fails closed — the current media segment finishes, the next is refused; audible stop within 10 s. Revocation is a deliberate leak response and does **not** inherit expiry's grace (`07.03.03` D-04) | Playback halts: "Access to this link has been withdrawn" |'  CONTRADICTED BY the next row, 07.05.02:102 — '| Link revoked while the recipient is mid-comment | Audio dies immediately; a comment whose composition began before revocation is accepted for **120 s** after. Losing feedback someone took the trouble to give is worse than a slightly late close (parent CX-01 Q5) | Comment posts with a note to the roster: "left after the link was revoked" |'  The rest of the file takes the 10 s reading — 07.05.02:142 — '| Revoked (sender/recipient) | Owner or creator revoked | Immediate; in-flight playback fails closed within 10 s; in-flight comments accepted 120 s |'; 07.05.02:206 — '| D-15 | Revocation **fails closed for audio** (next segment refused; audible stop ≤10 s) but **accepts an in-flight comment for 120 s** |'; 07.05.02:197 — '| D-06 | ... **Revocation does not inherit this grace** — it fails closed within 10 s, because revoking is a leak response, not a clock. |'
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building revocation reads row 102 and terminates the audio element instantly on the revoke event, cutting the recipient off mid-word and discarding the already-delivered segment. Row 101 and D-15 specify the opposite: let the in-flight segment play out and refuse the next one, bounded at 10 s. Because revocation is the platform's leak response, the two readings differ in exactly the property that matters — whether a segment already delivered to the client is allowed to finish — and only one of them is testable against D-15's '≤10 s' acceptance criterion.

findings.claim: The state-transition question for the sub-domain's highest-harm cross-cut — an undeclared sample surfacing after a public remix program is already live — is marked PENDING against a completed stage with no owner, and no decision in the child features covers the post-publication case.
findings.evidence: 07.08-delivery-readiness-qc-cx.md:110 — '5. **State transition conflict**: a sample declared after the program is live. The stems are already out and cannot be recalled. `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`'  The same CX block establishes the stakes — 07.08-delivery-readiness-qc-cx.md:107 — '2. **Trigger chain**: publish program → **must** verify source declarations first. This is the sub-domain's strongest candidate for a genuine hard block (sub-domain Q-01), because the harm lands on third parties who never consented to the risk.' and :102 — '- **Fan**: Read-only, and **the party harmed** — the only place in domain 07 where a Fan can be hurt by a provenance failure.'  The child's decisions cover only the pre-publication gate — 07.08.05-remix-stems-delivery-programs.md:110 — '| D-04 | Source declarations are **verified before publication** — the strongest hard-block candidate in the domain |' — and its irrevocability rule is written for the artist's own regret, not for a later declaration — 07.08.05:108 — '| D-02 | A public program is **irrevocable**, and the UI says so **before** the act |'; 07.08.05:65 — '| Artist publishes, then regrets it | **No undo exists.** The files are gone. The platform can stop *serving* them and cannot recall them | Warned unambiguously, before the act |'. Deferral target is a completed stage per ideation-index.md:65 ('Step 5 complete') and no owner is named.
findings.failureScenario: A sample is declared against a work after its stems are already published as a public remix program. Every downloader now holds material carrying an undisclosed third-party claim. The specification says only that the platform 'can stop serving them and cannot recall them' — written for the artist changing their mind, not for a newly surfaced clearance defect. An implementer must invent whether the late declaration halts serving, notifies prior downloaders, notifies the roster whose isolated performances are in circulation, marks the program's provenance record, or does nothing — a decision with third-party legal exposure, on the one surface the domain itself identifies as the only place a Fan can be harmed. The PENDING marker points at a stage that has already run and names no owner, so nothing downstream will resolve it.

findings.failureScenario: The audit rule for downstream consumers is to follow a cross-reference before treating detail as missing. These five references cannot be followed: three resolve above the ideation root and two name directories that no longer exist. A reader checking what domain 24 owns for abusive song renames, or what domain 20 renders from the contributor roster, hits a dead path and must guess the target — and the inconsistent treatment of domain 24 within the same sub-domain (one file correct, one stale) means the stale form cannot be recognised as a systematic typo from inside the file that carries it.
